source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר־הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה עִ֣יר עָז־לָ֔נוּ יְשׁוּעָ֥ה יָשִׁ֖ית חוֹמ֥וֹת וָחֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: In day that it will be sung, the song this, in [the] land of Judah: a city of strength [belongs] to us; salvation he sets [as] walls and rampart.

en.L: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: \q A city of strength [is] ours; \q salvation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets [as] walls and rampart.
en.B: On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judah: \q Ours is a mighty city; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raises salvation around it for wall and rampart.
en.R: At that time the people in the land of Judah will sing this song: \q Our city is strong! \q God surrounds it with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation, like walls and a fortress.

decisions.choice: a city of strength ... salvation as walls: the city God protects
decisions.reason: This city stands against the fallen city of 25:2 and 26:5. Its safety is not in stone but in God's salvation, as in 60:18, where the walls are named Salvation.

decisions.choice: he sets: God is the one who sets salvation in place
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; the song is about God (25:9), so he is the one who makes salvation the city's defense.

decisions.choice: rampart: the outer wall or bank before the main wall
decisions.reason: The word names the outer line of defense in front of a city wall (Lamentations 2:8; Nahum 3:8).

decisions.choice: God surrounds it with his salvation
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the subject and turns the walls into a comparison.

source.text: פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים וְיָבֹ֥א גוֹי־צַדִּ֖יק שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֱמֻנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Open gates so that it may enter, a nation righteous, keeping faithfulnesses.

en.L: Open [the] gates, \q so that a righteous nation may enter, [one that] keeps faithfulness.
en.B: Throw the gates wide, \q so a righteous nation may march in, one that remains faithful.
en.R: Open the city gates! \q Let a righteous nation come in, a people who stay faithful.

decisions.choice: open the gates so the righteous may enter: an entrance song
decisions.reason: Psalm 118:19-20 has the same pattern: "Open to me the gates of righteousness ... the righteous will enter it." Psalm 24:3-10 also asks who may enter God's place.

decisions.choice: keeping faithfulness: staying loyal and true
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, which stresses faithfulness in full. The nation keeps faith with God, unlike the faithless city of 1:21.

source.text: יֵ֣צֶר סָמ֔וּךְ תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: A mind firm you will keep peace, peace, for in you [he is] trusting.

en.L: [The] mind [that is] steadfast {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will keep [in] peace, peace, \q for in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [it is] trusting.
en.B: The mind that is held steady {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guard in peace, unbroken peace, \q for it relies on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Some people keep their minds steady by leaning on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because they trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You keep them safe in peace, peace that is full and complete.

decisions.choice: peace, peace: complete peace
decisions.reason: The word is doubled, which makes it whole and full, as in 57:19, "peace, peace to the far and the near". Jeremiah 6:14 uses the same doubling for a false promise of peace. The doubling is kept rather than turned into an adjective.

decisions.choice: a mind held steady: a settled purpose that leans on God
decisions.reason: The first word means what a person forms in the mind, purpose or inclination (Genesis 8:21; 1 Chronicles 29:18). The second means propped up or supported, and so firm (Psalm 112:8). The mind is steady because it rests on God.

decisions.choice: you will keep: guard and watch over
decisions.reason: The verb means to guard, as a watchman guards a city (27:3). The line opens with "mind" for emphasis; God guards the mind that trusts him.

decisions.choice: Some people keep their minds steady by leaning on you ... You keep them safe
decisions.reason: Readable describes the people first and then what God does for them, and explains "steady" as leaning on God, as m2 describes.

source.text: בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה צ֖וּר עוֹלָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Trust in Yahweh until perpetuity, for in Yah, Yahweh, [is] a rock of everlastingnesses.

en.L: Trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever, \q for in Yah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [is] a rock of ages.
en.B: Put your trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for all time, \q for Yah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is a rock that stands through every age.
en.R: Always trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because Yah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is like a rock that lasts forever.

decisions.choice: Yah, Yahweh: the short form of the divine name, then the name in full
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh (Exodus 15:2). As in 12:2, Isaiah sets the short and full names side by side for emphasis.

decisions.choice: in Yah ... a rock: Yah is the rock
alternatives: in Yah there is a rock
decisions.reason: The preposition "in" can mark what someone is (Exodus 6:3, "as God Almighty"), so the line says that Yah himself is the rock. It can also be read "in Yah there is a rock"; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: a rock of ages: an everlasting place of safety
decisions.reason: God is called a rock as a sure refuge that does not move (17:10; 30:29; 44:8; Deuteronomy 32:4). The plural "ages" stresses that he lasts through all time.

decisions.choice: Yah
decisions.reason: The short form is kept as "Yah", as in 12:2, so the reader can see the doubled name.

source.text: כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם קִרְיָ֖ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ עַד־אֶ֔רֶץ יַגִּיעֶ֖נָּה עַד־עָפָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: For he has laid low [the] inhabitants of height, a town set on high; he will bring it low, he will bring it low to ground; he will make it touch to dust.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought down [the] inhabitants of [the] height, \q [the] lofty town; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lays it low, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lays it low to [the] ground, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes it touch the dust.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has humbled those who lived on the heights, \q the city perched up high; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings it down, down to the ground, \q and lays it level with the dust.
en.R: He has brought down the people who lived up high. \q He has knocked down their city that stood so high. \q He has thrown it down to the ground, down into the dust.

decisions.choice: lay low ... bring low ... make touch the dust: the same verbs as 25:12
decisions.reason: The three verbs used for Moab's walls in 25:12 return here for the lofty city. What God did to Moab he does to every proud city.

decisions.choice: the lofty town: the proud, unnamed city
decisions.reason: The city is high in place and in pride, the kind of height God brings down in 2:12-17. It is the unnamed city of 24:10 and 25:2.

source.text: תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל רַגְלֵ֥י עָנִ֖י פַּעֲמֵ֥י דַלִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: It will trample it, a foot, [the] feet of [the] afflicted, [the] footsteps of poor [ones].

en.L: A foot will trample it, \q [the] feet of [the] afflicted, [the] steps of [the] poor.
en.B: It is trodden underfoot: \q the afflicted walk over it, and the weak tread its ruins.
en.R: Now the poor and the people who suffer walk all over it.

decisions.choice: the feet of the afflicted: the poor walk over the city that was proud
decisions.reason: God reverses the places of the proud and the poor (25:4; 14:30, 32). Mary's song speaks of the same reversal (Luke 1:52).

decisions.choice: the afflicted: those bowed down by poverty and oppression
decisions.reason: The word means poor, humbled and oppressed (3:14-15; 10:2).

decisions.choice: tread its ruins
decisions.reason: Balanced says "ruins" for what remains of the city of verse 5; Literal keeps "it".

source.text: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] way for the righteous [is] level paths; O upright [one], [the] track of [the] righteous you make level.

en.L: [The] path of the righteous [is] level paths; \q Upright [One], the track of [the] righteous {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make level.
en.B: For those who are righteous the road runs level; \q Upright One, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} smooth the track they walk.
en.R: You are the Upright One. \q You make the road smooth and level for people who are righteous.

decisions.choice: Upright One: a title of God, spoken to him
alternatives: you make the track of the righteous straight
decisions.reason: The word stands alone in the middle of the line and is best taken as addressing God, who is upright (Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 92:16). It may instead describe the path: "you make the track of the righteous straight".

decisions.choice: you make level: make smooth and even
decisions.reason: The verb means to level or make even, as in Proverbs 4:26 and 5:21, where it is used with the same word for track. God clears the way of the righteous of things that make them stumble (40:3-4).

source.text: אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also [in the] way of your judgments, O Yahweh, we have waited for you; for your name and for your memorial [is the] desire of soul.

en.L: Yes, [in] the path of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name and for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} remembrance [is the] desire of [our] soul.
en.B: Even on the path where {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments lead, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q our deepest longing is for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, the name by which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are remembered.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} while we followed the way of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments. \q More than anything, we long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name and to remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: your judgments: God's acts of judgment that put things right
decisions.reason: The word can mean laws or rulings, but here, as in verse 9, it means God's acts of judging the world. The people wait for God along the way his judgments take.

decisions.choice: your remembrance: the name by which God is remembered and called on
decisions.reason: The word is used with "name" for the name God gives himself (Exodus 3:15; Psalm 135:13).

decisions.choice: the desire of the soul: the longing of the whole self
decisions.reason: The word for soul means the whole living self; its desire is the deepest longing. "Our" is implied by "we" in the same verse.

source.text: נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֨יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: [With] my soul I have desired you in the night; also [with] my spirit in my inner being I will seek you earnestly; for when your judgments [are] to [the] earth, righteousness they learn, [the] inhabitants of [the] world.

en.L: [With] my soul I desire {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the night; \q also [with] my spirit within me I seek {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} earnestly; \q for when {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments [come] to the earth, \q the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
en.B: I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my being in the night, \q and my spirit within me searches eagerly for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q For whenever {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments reach the earth, \q the people of the world come to learn righteousness.
en.R: At night I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with my whole being. \q Deep inside me, my spirit searches hard for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.

decisions.choice: I seek you earnestly: search with eager desire
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek eagerly. It is related to the word for dawn, and some take it as "I seek you at dawn", which would answer "in the night" in the first line (Psalm 63:2).

decisions.choice: when your judgments come, the world learns righteousness
decisions.reason: God's judgments teach the nations what is right. Verse 10 gives the other side: kindness alone does not teach the wicked.

decisions.choice: my soul ... my spirit: the whole person
decisions.reason: The two words together mean the speaker's whole inner self, as in Psalm 77:4.

source.text: יֻחַ֤ן רָשָׁע֙ בַּל־לָמַ֣ד צֶ֔דֶק בְּאֶ֥רֶץ נְכֹח֖וֹת יְעַוֵּ֑ל וּבַל־יִרְאֶ֖ה גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: He is shown favor, [the] wicked, not he learns righteousness; in a land of uprightness he acts unjustly and not he sees the majesty of Yahweh.

en.L: [If] the wicked is shown favor, he does not learn righteousness; \q in a land of uprightness he acts unjustly \q and does not see the majesty of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Show mercy to the wicked, and still they will not learn righteousness; \q even where all is upright they act crookedly, \q blind to the majesty of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But when wicked people are treated kindly, they still do not learn righteousness. \q Even in a land where people do right, they keep doing wrong. \q They do not see how great {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is.

decisions.choice: if the wicked is shown favor, he does not learn: kindness alone does not teach the wicked
decisions.reason: The first verb stands without "if", but the line is a condition. It sets the wicked against the world of verse 9, which learns righteousness when God judges.

decisions.choice: the majesty of Yahweh: his lofty greatness
decisions.reason: The word means height or majesty, used of God's glorious deeds in 12:5. The wicked are blind to it.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a singular that stands for every wicked person; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

source.text: יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ בַּל־יֶחֱזָי֑וּן יֶחֱז֤וּ וְיֵבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ קִנְאַת־עָ֔ם אַף־אֵ֖שׁ צָרֶ֥יךָ תֹאכְלֵֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: O Yahweh, it is raised, your hand, not they behold; they will behold and they will be ashamed, [the] zeal of a people; also the fire [of] your foes it will consume them.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand [is] lifted high, [yet] they do not see; \q they will see and be ashamed [at the] zeal [for the] people; \q yes, the fire [for] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foes will consume them.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand is lifted up, yet they take no notice. \q They will see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning devotion to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, and shame will cover them; \q the very fire that waits for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies will devour them.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have raised {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand to act, but the wicked do not notice. \q They will see how deeply {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} care for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, and they will be ashamed. \q The fire meant for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies will burn them up.

decisions.choice: your hand is lifted high: God is ready to act
decisions.reason: A raised hand is ready to strike or to save (Micah 5:8). The wicked do not see that God is about to act.

decisions.choice: the zeal of a people: God's zeal for his people
decisions.reason: The two words can mean God's jealous love for his people (9:6; 37:32), which the wicked will see and be ashamed. They may instead mean the people's own zeal.

decisions.choice: the fire of your foes: the fire meant for your enemies
decisions.reason: The fire belongs to the enemies in the sense that it is prepared for them (33:11-14; Hebrews 10:27).

decisions.choice: the wicked; how deeply you care for
decisions.reason: Readable names "they" as the wicked of verse 10 and explains God's zeal as his deep care for his people.

source.text: יְהוָ֕ה תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ת שָׁל֖וֹם לָ֑נוּ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם כָּֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ינוּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: O Yahweh, you will establish peace for us, for also all our works you have done for us.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will establish peace for us, \q for also all our works {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done for us.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will set peace in place for us; \q indeed, whatever we have accomplished was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} doing for us.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will give us peace. \q In fact, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who did all our work for us.

decisions.choice: you will establish: set in place
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It is used for setting a pot on the fire (2 Kings 4:38; Ezekiel 24:3). God sets peace firmly in place for his people.

decisions.choice: all our works you have done for us: what God's people achieve is his work
decisions.reason: The people own that their deeds are God's doing on their behalf (Psalm 90:17; Philippians 2:13).

source.text: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָל֥וּנוּ אֲדֹנִ֖ים זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ לְבַד־בְּךָ֖ נַזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: O Yahweh, our God, they have ruled over us, lords except you; only in you we bring to remembrance your name.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, lords besides {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have ruled over us; \q [but] only by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do we call to mind {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, masters other than {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have lorded it over us, \q but it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, that we call on.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, in the past other rulers controlled us instead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the only one whose name we call on.

decisions.choice: lords: foreign rulers, and the gods behind them
decisions.reason: The word means masters or lords. It names the foreign kings who ruled Israel, such as Assyria and Babylon; it may also hint at other gods, since Baal means "lord".

decisions.choice: we bring to remembrance your name: call on your name in worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to mention or invoke a name, especially in praise and prayer (Psalm 20:8; Exodus 23:13).

decisions.choice: in the past
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the rule of other lords is past, as the verb form does.

source.text: מֵתִים֙ בַּל־יִחְי֔וּ רְפָאִ֖ים בַּל־יָקֻ֑מוּ לָכֵ֤ן פָּקַ֨דְתָּ֙ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וַתְּאַבֵּ֥ד כָּל־זֵ֖כֶר לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Dead [ones] not they will live; shades not they will rise; therefore you have visited and you have destroyed them, and you have destroyed all remembrance of them.

en.L: [The] dead will not live; shades will not rise; \q therefore {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have visited and destroyed them, \q and made all memory of them perish.
en.B: They are dead and will not live again; \q they are with the dead and will not rise. \q That is why {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} dealt with them, wiped them out, \q and erased every memory of them.
en.R: Those rulers are dead now and will never live again. \q They are with the dead and will never rise. \q You punished them and destroyed them. \q No one even remembers them anymore.

decisions.choice: shades: the dead in the world below
decisions.reason: The word names the weak, shadowy dead in Sheol (14:9; Psalm 88:11).

decisions.choice: the dead will not live: the oppressors are gone for good
decisions.reason: The dead here are the foreign lords of verse 13. Verse 19 answers this line: those lords will not rise, but God's own dead will live.

decisions.choice: therefore: the reason they lie dead
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore": because God punished them, they are dead and forgotten. It can also mean "surely" here.

decisions.choice: They are dead ... they are with the dead (Balanced); those rulers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both words mean the dead, and "the dead" is used for shades at Balanced and Readable; the two lines are turned so that both say it. Readable names the dead as the rulers of verse 13.

source.text: יָסַ֤פְתָּ לַגּוֹי֙ יְהוָ֔ה יָסַ֥פְתָּ לַגּ֖וֹי נִכְבָּ֑דְתָּ רִחַ֖קְתָּ כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: You have added to the nation, O Yahweh, you have added to the nation; you have gained glory; you have extended all [the] boundaries of [the] land.

en.L: You have added to the nation, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have added to the nation; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been glorified; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have extended all [the] borders of [the] land.
en.B: You have made the nation grow, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made the nation grow; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory \q and pushed out every border of the land.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made our nation bigger. \q Yes, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made it larger, and this brings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} glory. \q You have pushed back the borders of our land on every side.

decisions.choice: you have added to the nation: God has made his people many
decisions.reason: God promised to make Abraham's descendants many (Genesis 15:5), and Isaiah speaks of it in 9:2 and 54:2-3.

decisions.choice: you have extended all the borders of the land
alternatives: you have removed them far to the ends of the earth
decisions.reason: The verb means to make far. Most likely God has pushed the borders far out. It may instead mean that God has sent his people far away to the ends of the earth, in exile.

decisions.choice: our nation; our land
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the speakers' own nation and land are meant.

source.text: יְהוָ֖ה בַּצַּ֣ר פְּקָד֑וּךָ צָק֣וּן לַ֔חַשׁ מוּסָרְךָ֖ לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: O Yahweh, in distress they sought you; they poured out a whisper, your chastening [was] to them.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, in distress they sought {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q they poured out a whisper [when] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} discipline [was] on them.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when hardship came they sought {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} out; \q under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} correction they poured out a hushed prayer.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people were in trouble, they came looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} corrected them, they prayed to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} quietly.

decisions.choice: they poured out a whisper: a quiet prayer
decisions.reason: The line is hard: the verb is spelled unusually, and the noun can mean a whispered charm (3:3) or a whispered prayer. The sense "they poured out a whispered prayer" fits the context of seeking God.

decisions.choice: your chastening: your discipline
decisions.reason: The word means correction that teaches, as a father disciplines a son (Proverbs 3:11-12).

decisions.choice: your people
decisions.reason: Readable names "they" as God's people.

source.text: כְּמ֤וֹ הָרָה֙ תַּקְרִ֣יב לָלֶ֔דֶת תָּחִ֥יל תִּזְעַ֖ק בַּחֲבָלֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן הָיִ֥ינוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a pregnant [woman] [who] brings near to give birth, she is in labor, she cries out in her pangs, so we were from before you, O Yahweh.

en.L: Like a pregnant [woman who] draws near to give birth, \q [who] writhes [and] cries out in her pangs, \q so were we before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Like an expectant mother whose hour has come, \q who twists in pain and cries out in her labor, \q that is how we have been before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we were in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence like a woman about to have a baby, \q who twists in pain and screams with her labor pains.

decisions.choice: a woman in labor: a picture of anguish
decisions.reason: The prophets use the pains of childbirth for the deepest distress (13:8; 21:3; Jeremiah 30:6). Verse 18 adds that the pain brought nothing to birth.

decisions.choice: before you: in your presence
decisions.reason: The words mean in God's presence, and may also mean "because of you", that is, under God's discipline of verse 16.

source.text: הָרִ֣ינוּ חַ֔לְנוּ כְּמ֖וֹ יָלַ֣דְנוּ ר֑וּחַ יְשׁוּעֹת֙ בַּל־נַ֣עֲשֶׂה אֶ֔רֶץ וּבַֽל־יִפְּל֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: We were pregnant, we were in labor; as it were we gave birth to wind; deliverances not we accomplish [for the] earth, and not they fall, the inhabitants of [the] world.

en.L: We were pregnant, we writhed; as it were, we gave birth to wind; \q deliverances we did not accomplish [for the] earth, \q and [the] inhabitants of [the] world did not fall [into birth].
en.B: We conceived and labored, but it was as if we bore only wind. \q We have won no deliverance for the earth, \q and no new inhabitants of the world have been born.
en.R: We were like a pregnant woman in pain, but nothing was born. It was as if we gave birth to wind. \q We have not brought salvation to the earth. \q No new people have been born into the world.

decisions.choice: we gave birth to wind: all the pain produced nothing
decisions.reason: Wind stands for what is empty and useless (41:29; Hosea 8:7).

decisions.choice: deliverances: victories that rescue
decisions.reason: The word is the one for salvation, in the plural; the people could not bring rescue to the earth by their own effort.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of the world did not fall: no one was born
alternatives: the inhabitants of the world did not fall (in defeat)
decisions.reason: To "fall" can mean to be born, as a child drops at birth; verse 19 uses the same verb for the earth giving birth to the dead. It may instead mean that the people of the world, the enemy, did not fall.

source.text: יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They will live, your dead; my corpse, they will rise; awake and shout for joy, dwellers of dust! For [the] dew of lights [is] your dew, and [the] earth [the] shades it will make fall.

en.L: Your dead will live; my corpse[s] will rise. \q Awake and shout for joy, dwellers in [the] dust! For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dew [is] a dew of lights, \q and [the] earth will give birth to [the] shades.
en.B: Your dead will live; my dead bodies will rise. \q Wake up and shout with gladness, you who lie in the dust! For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dew is a dew of shining light, \q and the earth will bring the dead to birth.
en.R: The people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and have died will live again. Our dead bodies will rise. \q You who lie in the dust, wake up and shout with joy! Your dew is like the bright morning dew that makes plants live again, \q and the earth will give back the dead.

decisions.choice: your dead ... my corpse: the people speak to God
decisions.reason: The prayer of verses 11-18 is spoken to God, so "your dead" are those who belong to God, and "my corpse" is the speaking people's own dead, taken as a group. The speaker may instead be God, speaking to Israel of its dead.

decisions.choice: your dead will live: the dead of God's people will rise
decisions.reason: This answers verse 14: the foreign lords will not rise, but God's own dead will. Daniel 12:2 takes up the picture of those asleep in the dust who will awake.

decisions.choice: a dew of lights ... the earth will give birth to the shades
alternatives: you make the dew fall on the land of the shades
decisions.reason: Dew brings dry ground back to life (Hosea 14:6); "lights" most likely means the light of dawn. The last verb means to make fall, as at birth (verse 18): the earth gives birth to the dead. It can also be read "you will make it fall on the land of the shades", that is, the dew falls on the dead. The word for lights may instead mean herbs (2 Kings 4:39).

decisions.choice: the people who belong to you; our dead bodies; that makes plants live again
decisions.reason: Readable explains "your dead" and "my corpse" as m1 reads them, and explains the picture of the dew.

source.text: לֵ֤ךְ עַמִּי֙ בֹּ֣א בַחֲדָרֶ֔יךָ וּֽסְגֹ֥ר דְּלָתְךָ֖ בַּעֲדֶ֑ךָ חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־רֶ֖גַע עַד־יַעֲבָר־זָֽעַם׃

records.literal_gloss: Come, my people, go in your rooms and shut your door[s] behind you; hide like a little moment until it has passed by, indignation.

en.L: Go, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, enter into your rooms and shut your doors behind you; \q hide for a little moment until [the] wrath passes by.
en.B: Come, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, step inside your rooms and bar the doors behind you. \q Keep hidden for a short while, until the wrath has gone past.
en.R: My people, go into your homes and shut the doors. \q Hide for a little while, until God's anger has passed.

decisions.choice: shut your doors ... until the wrath passes by: as at the Passover
decisions.reason: At the first Passover, Israel stayed inside behind closed doors until the destroyer had passed by (Exodus 12:22-23).

decisions.choice: indignation: God's wrath against the world
decisions.reason: The word is used for God's fierce anger in judgment (10:5, 25; 13:5).

decisions.choice: God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable names whose anger it is; the next verse shows the LORD coming out to judge.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן יֹֽשֵׁב־הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֑יו וְגִלְּתָ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶת־דָּמֶ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־תְכַסֶּ֥ה ע֖וֹד עַל־הֲרוּגֶֽיהָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For here! Yahweh [is] about to go forth from his place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitant[s] of the earth on him; and it will reveal, the earth, its blood[s], and not it will cover still over its slain.

en.L: For look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] about to go out from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place \q to visit the iniquity of the inhabitants of the earth on them; \q and the earth will uncover its blood \q and will no longer cover its slain.
en.B: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is setting out from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place \q to call the people of the earth to account for their guilt. \q The earth will lay bare the blood poured out on it \q and no longer keep its slain covered.
en.R: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is leaving {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home in heaven to punish the people of the earth for their sin. \q The earth will show the blood of people who were murdered. \q It will not hide those who were killed any longer.

decisions.choice: about to go out from his place: God comes to judge
decisions.reason: Micah 1:3 uses almost the same words: "the LORD is coming out from his place." His place is his dwelling in heaven or his temple.

decisions.choice: visit the iniquity: punish the guilt
decisions.reason: To visit iniquity on someone is to call them to account for it (13:11; 24:21).

decisions.choice: the earth will uncover its blood: hidden murders exposed
decisions.reason: Spilled blood cries out from the ground for justice (Genesis 4:10-11; Job 16:18). When God comes, the earth will hide no murder any longer.

decisions.choice: his home in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable explains "his place"; it may instead be his temple (m1).
